decisions.difference: A: (Difficulty talking)  vs  B: (Difficulty talking + Sudden onset)
decisions.reason: "New sudden" qualifies the weakness/numbness clause; "difficulty speaking" follows a semicolon without it, so the unqualified form is closer to the words.

decisions.difference: A: (and (Headache + Worsening) (Frequent headache))  vs  B: (Frequent headache + Worsening)
decisions.reason: "Getting worse and more frequent" names two properties joined by "and"; A encodes each, B's single concept reads as a frequent headache that worsens.

decisions.difference: A: (Wakes up during night)  vs  B: not encoded
decisions.reason: "Headache that wakes patient" is a red-box item; A's concept (already in VHA's vocabulary) approximates it inside the headache rule, whereas B drops it entirely.

decisions.difference: A: (and (Headache + Chronic persistent) (Procedure: Highly active antiretroviral therapy))  vs  B: not encoded
decisions.final_expr: (and (clinical_finding Headache (qualifier Chronic persistent)) (finding Procedure Highly active antiretroviral therapy))
decisions.reason: "Persistent headache since starting ART" is a red-box item; A's encoding passes all checks and uses a concept already in VHA's vocabulary, so it is kept with "since" recorded as not modelled.

decisions.difference: A: not present  vs  B: (Clouded consciousness)
decisions.reason: "Drowsy/confused": Clouded consciousness is VHA's common term for confusion and sits beside Acute confusion, so both record forms of "confused" count.

decisions.difference: A: (Purulent nasal discharge)  vs  B: (Nasal discharge + Thick)
decisions.reason: The page says "thick nasal ... discharge", not purulent; B uses the page's word.

A: (Tightness sensation @ Head structure)  vs  B: (Tightening pain @ Head structure)
decisions.reason: "Tightness around head" matches Tightness sensation; the page lists pain separately ("or generalised pressure-like pain").

decisions.difference: A: (Aching headache + Continuous)  vs  B: (Aching pain + Continuous)
decisions.reason: The page says "constant aching pain"; B uses the page's words, and the rule's Headache condition keeps the headache context.

decisions.difference: A: (Tenderness @ Entire skeletal muscle of neck)  vs  B: (Tenderness @ Skeletal muscle structure of neck)
decisions.reason: "Tender neck muscles" is any part of the neck muscles; the structure concept (both resolve) fits better than the "entire" concept.

decisions.difference: A: (SBP >= 180 or DBP >= 110) without the pregnancy clause  vs  B: (and (SBP >= 180 or DBP >= 110) (no Pregnancy))
decisions.final_expr: (>= SBP 180) / (>= DBP 110) as members of the red-box or
decisions.reason: Inside the red-box "or" a pregnant patient with BP >= 180/110 already meets "Pregnant ... and BP >= 140/90", so dropping "and not pregnant" leaves the urgent result unchanged, whereas B's (no Pregnancy) misses men and anyone without a recorded "not pregnant".

decisions.difference: A: Spotted fever group rickettsial disease  vs  B: African tick bite fever
decisions.reason: The page writes "tick bite fever", which matches African tick bite fever by name; whether it is also meant to cover Boutonneuse fever (A's broader parent) the page does not say.

decisions.difference: A: not encoded  vs  B: possible Acute viral disease when Q0 = Yes, sinusitis branch absent and no tick bite

decisions.reason: The page names a diagnosis for the "none of above" branch ("treat as acute viral infection"); "treat as" is neither "likely" nor "consider", so it is kept at possible and the malaria exclusion cannot be modelled.

decisions.reason: Both are topic-specific and unique; the base build's names are kept (acute viral infection takes the same pattern).
